clue.text: Mad non-scientist lacking method

indicators.note: something mad is crazed and disordered, so the letters next to it are scrambled

parts.note: taken letter for letter, ignoring the hyphen

explanation.surface: A crank with no scientific training whose reasoning follows no method at all.
explanation.walkthrough: The twelve letters of NON-SCIENTIST rearrange exactly into INCONSISTENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done without any steady system or rule is inconsistent, erratic from one time to the next.

clue.text: Compose rising melody for sea power

indicators.note: in a down entry rising means reading upwards, so the word is turned around

parts.note: to pen is to write or compose
a tune is a melody

explanation.surface: Writing an ascending tune to celebrate naval strength.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sea power' suggests a navy, but it is the Roman god of the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Neptune is the Roman god ruling the oceans, a deity whose power is over the sea.

clue.text: Clothed in taffeta, I posed opposite 8

indicators.note: opposite means facing the other way, so the concealed letters are read backwards
something clothed in fabric is wrapped inside it, so the answer lies within these words

parts.note: the run of letters spanning the end of taffeta through I and into posed

explanation.surface: Dressed in taffeta, a model strikes a pose facing someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 8 refers to 8-down, NARCOTIC, which serves as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An opiate is a drug derived from opium that dulls the senses, a narcotic.

clue.text: European southwest is slow, at first

parts.note: the compass abbreviation
taken as written

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter of the preceding word

parts.note: its opening letter

explanation.surface: A remark that a southwestern European is sluggish to begin with.
explanation.walkthrough: SW + IS + S.
explanation.definitionFit: A Swiss person is a native of Switzerland, a country in central Europe.

clue.text: Dress a piece of eggplant in animal fat and sweet vegetable

indicators.note: in places the clothing and the letter inside the fat word

parts.note: suet is hard animal fat
garb is clothing, dress

indicators.note: a piece means just one letter, the first, of the following word

parts.note: its opening letter

explanation.surface: A recipe: coat a slice of aubergine in animal fat and serve with a sweet root.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dress' looks like a cooking verb, as in dressing a salad, but here it means clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Sugar beet is a root crop grown for its high sugar content, so it is a sweet vegetable.

clue.text: Commercial in gym supports poor case for stunt

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece stands underneath, so it comes after the other
something poor is in bad shape, so the letters of the next word are disordered

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the commercial sits in the gym, inside its letters

parts.note: PE is physical education, school gym class
an ad is a commercial

explanation.surface: An advertisement filmed in a gym backs a weak argument in favour of a stunt.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry the supporting piece goes underneath, so the gym-and-commercial unit comes last.
explanation.definitionFit: An escapade is a daring or reckless adventure, a stunt or prank.

clue.text: Excessive sensitivity about mantra

indicators.note: about means around, so the sensitivity word encircles the mantra

parts.note: touch as a delicate sensitivity, as in a light touch
om is the sacred syllable chanted as a mantra

explanation.surface: Being overly sensitive about one's chanted phrase.
explanation.walkthrough: Om is the sacred syllable of Hindu and Buddhist meditation, the classic mantra.
explanation.definitionFit: Too much means more than is reasonable, an excessive amount.

clue.text: Sleep-inducing acorn cooked to overcome spasm

indicators.note: in a down clue overcoming means sitting on top, so the cooked letters come first
cooking transforms ingredients, so the nut's letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written
a tic is a twitching spasm

explanation.surface: A soothing remedy made from cooked acorns that calms muscle spasms.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, overcoming puts one piece on top, so the cooked letters come before the spasm.
explanation.definitionFit: Narcotic as an adjective describes drugs that dull the senses and induce sleep, its original meaning.

clue.text: Finishes off homework in little bookie joint

indicators.note: the finishes of the following words are their last letters, which are kept

parts.note: the final letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: Someone completes their homework in a small betting shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' looks like part of 'bookie joint', a betting den, but it is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: The knee is the hinge joint between thigh and lower leg.

clue.text: Getting up to follow news service at start of press briefing

indicators.note: the getting-up word is told to come after the earlier pieces rather than lead

parts.note: the Associated Press, a US news agency

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the following word is wanted here

parts.note: its opening letter
getting up from bed or a seat

explanation.surface: A wire-service report on people rising to their feet, at the start of a press briefing.
explanation.walkthrough: AP, then P, then RISING: APPRISING.
explanation.definitionFit: To apprise someone is to inform them, so apprising is briefing them, as a participle.

clue.text: A pair of climatologists acknowledge someone with big shoes to fill

definitions.text: someone with big shoes to fill

indicators.note: a pair means two, so just the first two letters of the next word are taken

parts.note: its first two letters
to own up to something is to acknowledge it

explanation.surface: Two climate scientists pay tribute to a predecessor whose legacy will be hard to live up to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Someone with big shoes to fill' reads as an idiom for an impressive predecessor, but here it is literal: a clown wears huge floppy shoes.
explanation.definitionFit: Circus clowns famously wear outsized shoes, so the phrase is taken literally as a playful description.

clue.text: Nobleman to read characters in front of this clue and above this puzzle, one after the other

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a European noble ranking like an earl

definitions.text: read characters in front of this clue and above this puzzle, one after the other
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the clue number 12 and the puzzle number 3456 read in sequence go 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6

explanation.walkthrough: The characters in front of the clue are its number, 12, and above the puzzle stands its number, 3456; reading them in order recites the numbers one to six.
explanation.definitionFit: A continental aristocrat is titled a count, and to say numbers in sequence is also to count.

clue.text: Gang member, at wit's end, captivated by certain books of the Bible

indicators.note: something captivated is held captive, so these letters sit inside another word

parts.note: sure means certain
the Crips are a Los Angeles street gang

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, the only one kept

parts.note: its final letter

explanation.surface: A gangster at the end of his tether is gripped by particular books of the Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: The Crips are a well-known Los Angeles street gang, so a member is a Crip.
explanation.definitionFit: Scripture is the sacred writing of the Bible, the collection of its books.

clue.text: Class for one learning macramé?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a rank or level
second meaning, whimsical: macramé is knotted cord, so its student is one who ties

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the made-up second sense, someone who ties knots, rhyming with 'fire' not 'fear'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tier is a level or grade, a class in a ranked arrangement such as seating or pricing.

clue.text: Bond fanatics, having run with it

indicators.note: to have something is to hold it, so the fanatics word holds another letter

parts.note: fiends are devotees, as in fitness fiends
R is the cricket and baseball abbreviation for run
hip means fashionable, with it

explanation.surface: Fans of James Bond who have been hurrying along with the times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond' tempts as 007, but it means a tie between people.
explanation.definitionFit: A friendship is a bond of affection between people, a tie of mutual loyalty.

clue.text: Comes back to harvest fruit

parts.note: to reap is to harvest
pears are fruit

explanation.surface: Someone returns home to gather the orchard crop.
explanation.walkthrough: REAP + PEARS.
explanation.definitionFit: To reappear is to show up again, so something that reappears returns.

clue.text: Slithering serpents' sass

indicators.note: slithering is twisting and writhing, so these letters wriggle into a new order

parts.note: taken as written; the possessive is ignored

explanation.surface: The cheek of snakes slipping along.
explanation.definitionFit: Pertness is cheeky boldness, the same impudence that sass names in American usage.

clue.text: Frequently last talent — so sad

indicators.note: something in a sad state is in a sorry mess, so the preceding letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lament that a fading talent is so often the last one picked.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the stock phrase 'last but not least': the word last is frequently followed by not least.
explanation.definitionFit: In the idiom 'last but not least', the phrase routinely accompanies the word last, so it is what last frequently comes with.

clue.text: California diatribes involving Republicans: "They have deep pockets"

parts.note: the US postal abbreviation for California

indicators.note: to involve is to wrap up within, so the diatribes word encloses the party

parts.note: a diatribe is an angry rant
the Grand Old Party, the US Republican Party

explanation.surface: Political tirades in California involving Republicans, who are said to be rich donors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deep pockets' suggests wealthy backers, but the pockets are literal.
explanation.definitionFit: Cargo pants are loose trousers with large patch pockets on the thighs, so they literally have deep pockets.

clue.text: On reflection, we invested originally in guns and pans sometimes

indicators.note: in places the reflected letters inside the word for guns

parts.note: to gun an engine is to rev it

indicators.note: originally points to the very start of the preceding word, its first letter

parts.note: its opening letter

indicators.note: a reflection shows things back to front, so the letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Looking back, we put money into firearms and cookware now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guns' and 'pans' look like weapons and cookware but are verbs: to gun an engine, to pan a show.
explanation.definitionFit: A pan is a harsh critical write-up, so pans are one kind of reviews, hence 'sometimes'.

clue.text: Agitate in prison

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to ... up or ... a liquid
second meaning: slang 'in ...' means behind bars

explanation.walkthrough: Stir is old slang for prison, so 'in prison' is 'in stir'; the definition carries its own 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: To stir is to agitate or disturb, and stir is also slang for a jail.

clue.text: Early explorer of America raised company's killer crop

indicators.note: in a down entry raising means reading upwards, so the explorer's name runs backwards

parts.note: John Cabot reached North America in 1497
CO is the abbreviation for company; the 's joins

explanation.surface: An early explorer of America grew a firm's deadly crop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raised' suggests growing a crop, but it turns the explorer upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: Tobacco is a cultivated plant whose smoked leaf causes many deaths, a lethal harvest.

clue.text: Late summer breeze after a reversal of direction

indicators.note: after means coming later in sequence, so the breeze word follows the other pieces

parts.note: taken as written
a U-turn reverses one's direction
a gust is a sudden breeze

explanation.surface: A late-summer wind picks up after the wind direction changes.
explanation.walkthrough: A + U + GUST. U stands for a U-turn, the about-face of direction.
explanation.definitionFit: August is the final full month of summer in the northern hemisphere, so late summer.

clue.text: Warsaw native heads west, amid seven tangled wrappers

indicators.note: across clues read left to right, so heading west means reading the word right to left
amid means in the middle of, so one piece is placed inside the other
a tangled number word has its letters jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
Warsaw is in Poland, so a native is a Pole

explanation.surface: A man from Warsaw travels west wrapped in seven knotted layers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heads west' sounds like a journey, but in an across entry it means reading right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: Envelopes are paper covers that enclose letters, so they are wrappers.

clue.text: Engages oddly with roe

indicators.note: oddly means taking the letters in the odd positions, first, third and so on

parts.note: its first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.surface: Someone strangely gets involved with fish roe.
explanation.definitionFit: Roe is the mass of eggs inside a female fish, so the two are the same thing.

clue.text: Leaders of Saudi Arabia's neighbor are around _____!

definitions.text: Leaders of Saudi Arabia's neighbor are around _____!

indicators.note: the leaders of a group of words are their opening letters

parts.note: the first letter of each of the five words

explanation.surface: A fill-in-the-blank: where would you find the government of the country next to Saudi Arabia?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the leaders of Yemen, which borders Saudi Arabia, sit in its capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanaa is the capital of Yemen, the neighbour where that country's leaders are based.

clue.text: Metropolitan headdress is timeless

indicators.note: read as time-less, it asks for the headdress word without its time letter

parts.note: a turban is a wound cloth headdress
T is the standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A city-style headdress is described as timeless, a classic look.
explanation.walkthrough: The word 'timeless' splits as 'time' plus 'less': TURBAN without T leaves URBAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Urban means relating to a city, which is what metropolitan describes.

clue.text: Flip conclusion of terrific woman

indicators.note: flipping the ending swaps the final two letters of the following word

parts.note: great means terrific

explanation.surface: A flippant remark about the end of a terrific woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the last two letters of GREAT gives GRETA, as in Greta Garbo.
explanation.definitionFit: Greta is a female first name, so it stands for a woman in crossword style.

clue.text: Proclaims, "Coulter's a lightweight on the inside"

indicators.note: something on the inside sits within, so the weight unit goes into the name

parts.note: Ann Coulter is a US conservative pundit; her name plus the S
an ounce is a small unit of weight

explanation.surface: Someone declares that the pundit Ann Coulter is, deep down, a lightweight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lightweight' looks like an insult but is a unit of weight.
explanation.definitionFit: To announce something is to declare it publicly, which is what proclaiming means.

clue.text: A challenge for juniors is clique's fulfillment

parts.note: US high-school juniors sit the SAT college entrance exam
taken as written
a faction is a clique within a group; the 's is a joining possessive

explanation.surface: Teen-style wisdom: getting into the in-crowd is the real achievement for juniors.
explanation.walkthrough: The SAT is the American college entrance exam, typically taken in the junior year of high school.
explanation.definitionFit: Satisfaction is the contentment of a wish met, which is what fulfillment means.
